result.target_topic: Hedge De-designation Accounting and Portfolio Layer Method
result.target_summary: Upon de-designation, basis adjustments are amortized to interest income/expense over the remaining life. For certain AFS securities, the portfolio layer method allows hedging of prepayable and non-prepayable assets at the portfolio level with basis adjustments maintained until de-designation events, with the hedged amount being the sum of notional amounts of outstanding layers.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of ASU 2022-01 Portfolio Layer Method and HTM to AFS Transfer
comparisons.peer_summary: The company adopted ASU No. 2022-01 effective January 1, 2023, expanding hedging guidance to allow multiple hedge layers. Coincident with adoption, Citi transferred approximately $3.3 billion (amortized cost) of HTM mortgage-backed securities to AFS and hedged them under the new portfolio-layer method.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and C discuss the adoption and application of ASU No. 2022-01 (Portfolio Layer Method). MS discloses the application of this method to certain AFS securities, allowing both prepayable and non-prepayable assets. C provides context on the adoption of this ASU, noting it expands hedging guidance to allow multiple hedge layers and permitting the transfer of HTM securities to AFS to be hedged under this method, highlighting a shared regulatory driver and accounting framework.

sentences.text: For certain AFS securities, the Firm also applies the portfolio layer method of hedge accounting, which permits prepayable and non-prepayable assets to be included in the portfolio and allows more of the portfolio to be hedged.

Specifically, the guidance expands the current single-layer method to allow multiple hedge layers of a single closed portfolio of qualifying assets, which include both prepayable and non-prepayable assets.

Upon the adoption of the guidance, entities may elect to reclassify securities held-to-maturity to the available-for-sale category provided that the reclassified securities are designated in a portfolio hedge.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting treatment for interest rate fair value hedges
comparisons.peer_summary: For qualifying interest rate fair value hedges, gains or losses on derivatives and the hedging adjustment to the carrying value of hedged items are included in interest income/expense, with remaining differences amortized using the effective interest method upon de-designation.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS describe the accounting treatment upon de-designation of fair value hedges, specifically noting that remaining basis adjustments are amortized to interest income/expense over the remaining life using the effective interest method. MS states basis adjustments are amortized via the effective interest method upon de-designation, while GS states any remaining difference between carrying value and par value is amortized in interest income/expense over the remaining life using the effective interest method.

sentences.text: When a derivative is de-designated as a hedge, any basis adjustment remaining on the hedged asset (liability) is amortized to Interest income (expense) over the remaining life of the asset (liability) using the effective interest method.

When a derivative is no longer designated as a hedge, any remaining difference between the carrying value and par value of the hedged item is amortized in interest income/expense over the remaining life of the hedged item using the effective interest method.

comparisons.peer_topic: Portfolio layer method for interest rate risk
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm employs the portfolio layer method to manage interest rate risk of fixed-rate asset portfolios, maintaining basis adjustments at the portfolio level unless the portfolio falls below hedged layers or de-designation occurs.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPM explicitly discuss the application of the 'portfolio layer method' for hedging interest rate risk. MS notes that for certain AFS securities, this method permits prepayable and non-prepayable assets to be included in the portfolio and allows basis adjustments to be maintained at the portfolio level. Similarly, JPM employs the portfolio layer method to manage interest rate risk of fixed-rate asset portfolios, maintaining basis adjustments at the portfolio level unless specific de-designation events or portfolio shortfalls occur.

sentences.text: For certain AFS securities, the Firm also applies the portfolio layer method of hedge accounting, which permits prepayable and non-prepayable assets to be included in the portfolio and allows more of the portfolio to be hedged.

Further, the portfolio layer method of accounting requires that basis adjustments are maintained at the portfolio level and not allocated to individual items until certain de-designation events occur.
The Firm employs the portfolio layer method to manage the interest rate risk of portfolios of fixed-rate assets.
Throughout the life of the open hedge, basis adjustments are maintained at the portfolio level and are only allocated to individual assets under certain circumstances.

comparisons.peer_topic: Amortized cost and basis adjustments for portfolio layer method
comparisons.peer_summary: For portfolio layer method closed portfolios, the amortized cost was $72.8 billion and $83.9 billion, with designated hedged amounts and cumulative basis adjustments of $(1.7) billion and $(165) million at Dec 31, 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPM define how the hedged amount is determined under the portfolio layer method. MS states the designated hedged amount is the sum of the notional amounts of all outstanding layers in each portfolio. JPM confirms this same definition, stating the amount designated as hedged is the sum of the notional amounts of all outstanding layers, including spot and forward starting layers.

sentences.text: The amount designated as hedged is the sum of the notional amounts of all outstanding layers in each portfolio.
The amount designated as hedged is the sum of the notional amounts of all outstanding layers in each portfolio, which includes both spot starting and forward starting layers.
